about: scripts/perf-guard.py, small-project part: a cold haxeon build and haxeon check of tests/perf/small-project with the CLI built from the checkout, from no compile server running to the server's exit: the CLI's start and its project resolution, the server's start and the compile. Two modes, each with metrics of its own: vm_*, always measured, with haxeon-aot set aside so the VM runs the CLI's and the server's bytecode; aot_*, measured only when the CLI and compiler built ahead of time (haxeon-aot, haxeon dev aot) are current, which run the CLI and serve the compile, and skipped otherwise. The CLI's digest store is the guard's own, filled by an unmeasured build before the measured ones, each on a fresh copy of the project; the empty_store metrics measure one more build with it emptied. Measured on Linux x86-64; scripts/perf-guard.py --update writes the metrics that improved beyond their tolerance, --raise=METRIC=REASON one that is higher on purpose with its reason (raise_reason), in the commit that moves it. Tolerances are fractions of the value (tolerance) or counts (tolerance_abs).

vm_build_instructions.why: Instructions of every process the build starts on the VM, from perf: startup, which dominates a small project's build, and the compile. Compared only where perf is installed and allowed.
vm_build_instructions.raise_reason: the commits bisected for aot_build_instructions: ac8a1069b's KeyValueIterable typing of Map and Array for every program and d76d07a0f's collection after each compile's response, counted because the measurement runs until the server exits (VM not bisected separately)

vm_build_allocated_bytes.why: What the compile server on the VM allocated for the build (its worker allocations): deterministic for a given compiler and project.
vm_build_allocated_bytes.raise_reason: 41a2453b8 seeds every module typing can call (haxeon.DynamicOps, Reflect, Std, runtime.FloatBits, haxe.Int64) into the graph instead of restarting the frontend, so a cold server parses and types them for every program; 48c1b7aee brings the stdlib modules of the Bytes platform methods with haxe.io.Bytes the same way; 540848a15 (recorded reads) took part of it back (build about +1.7 and +0.7 MB); then stdlib typed in every program: 8b5e8403e (keyValueIterator on Array, Map and String, +0.4 MB), 0bf8f03af (Std's map formatter, +1.1 MB), ac8a1069b (ObjectMap's iteration methods nest V in {key, value}, so JsonPrinter's ObjectMap<Dynamic, Bool> is a specialized owner typed for every program, +2.2 MB after 07b95ac10 took back its repeated owner walks); 4ff774d3e's AST fields +0.3 MB after d3bb11835; smaller steps under 0.4 MB

vm_check_instructions.why: As vm_build_instructions, for a check, which types the project without writing a module.

aot_build_instructions.why: Instructions of every process the build starts with haxeon-aot, from perf: startup, which dominates a small project's build, and the compile. Compared only where perf is installed and allowed.
aot_build_instructions.raise_reason: ac8a1069b types Map and Array as KeyValueIterables for every program (+40M, with its allocation); d76d07a0f's full collection after each compile's response, off the build's path (wall unchanged), counted because the measurement runs until the server exits (+63M: main without it measures 1.564G); 4ff774d3e's API model grows the AOT image every process start pays (+14M); 07b95ac10 took back 9M (bisected over 25 commits from ccd159f11)
